subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and how should it treat failed mutating tools when the final assistant reply appears successful?
rationale: The UX gap is source-reproducible, but the fix changes public config and safety behavior for failed side effects, so automation should not choose the contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Opt-In Delivery Enum
options.body: Introduce a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off`, preserve current behavior as the default, and cover final-only/off behavior in payload, progress, docs, and config tests.

options.title: Keep Boolean-Only Policy
options.body: Document `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off operator escape hatch and decline success-aware delivery until stronger safety criteria exist.

options.title: Move Policy To Channels
options.body: Let team-chat plugins own warning visibility rules where channel UX differs, avoiding another global message config key.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Delivery Enum
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off`, preserve current behavior as the default, and cover final-only/off behavior in payload, progress, docs, and config tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest inspected current-main and merged-PR history around this warning-policy path and the related PRs that left this broader issue open.
